title: Compact-support projection formula on pro-etale sites with arbitrary finite l-primary coefficients
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^nR=0$ for some $n\geq1$; no flatness over $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ and no presentation of $R$ as a quotient of a discrete valuation ring is assumed. Let $X$, $\bar X$ and $Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$ be an open immersion and $p:\bar X\to Y$ a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-proper-morphism], and put $f=p\circ j$. Use the ordinary, uncompleted, unbounded derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ of module sheaves over the constant ring $R_T$ on the small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], their K-flat derived tensor product $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_R$ [def-weil-derived-tensor], the derived inverse and direct images with their adjunctions $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], and extension by zero $j_!$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero]; put $Rf_{!,R}=Rp_*j_!$.

For $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$ let $\operatorname{PF}_{R;M,K}$ be the composite
$$
Rf_{!,R}M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RK=(Rp_*j_!M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RK\xrightarrow{\ \pi_p\ }Rp_*\bigl(j_!M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RLp^*K\bigr)\xrightarrow{\ Rp_*(\pi_j)\ }Rp_*j_!\bigl(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RLj^*Lp^*K\bigr)\cong Rf_{!,R}\bigl(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RLf^*K\bigr),
$$
where $\pi_p$ is the proper projection map (the adjoint transpose under $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$ of the counit $Lp^*Rp_*j_!M\to j_!M$ tensored with $1_{Lp^*K}$, after the pullback/tensor comparison $Lp^*(V\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RW)\cong Lp^*V\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RLp^*W$), $\pi_j:j_!M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RN\to j_!(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_Rj^{-1}N)$ is the canonical extension-by-zero projection map with $N=Lp^*K$, and the last identification is the composition isomorphism $Lj^*Lp^*\cong Lf^*$.

If $M$ and $K$ have intrinsically constructible cohomology sheaves [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] vanishing outside a finite range of degrees, then $\operatorname{PF}_{R;M,K}$ is an isomorphism in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},R)$, natural in $M$ and $K$.

proof.text: Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ for the exact comparison from ordinary etale to ordinary pro-etale constant-$R$ module derived categories. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], choose bounded constructible etale complexes $M_0,K_0$ and isomorphisms $A_XM_0\cong M$, $A_YK_0\cong K$. This applies to the given arbitrary finite commutative ring $R$ and to intrinsic constructibility, with no Tor hypothesis. Fix these isomorphisms for the argument; the morphism whose invertibility is being tested remains the specified canonical one.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived; restriction to bounded objects

proof.text: Put $E=j^{\mathrm{et}}_!M_0$. Etale extension by zero acts degreewise on the derived category by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]; pro-etale extension by zero is also exact and acts degreewise by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. Apply the sheaf comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] in every degree. Because these functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms, its termwise inverse descends as well, giving $A_{\bar X}E\cong j_!A_XM_0\cong j_!M$. Thus $j_!M$ has this explicit etale origin, without assuming finite Tor amplitude or that its later tensor product is bounded below.

Use the already proved fixed-coefficient derived comparison square in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.ProEtale.FiniteCoefficient.Derived.LowerStarProjComparison. Its tensor compatibility is comparisonCompatible_leftDerivedComparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso. Work in ModuleCat (ULift R), which has functorial flat resolutions, and put H = E tensor-derived Lp* K0. These unbounded derived functors require no finite Tor amplitude. No general ringed-topos tensor comparison statement is needed.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; comparison square for nu and p

proof.text: The ring $R$ is torsion since $\ell^nR=0$, and $p$ is proper. Therefore [lem-kun-0f0g] makes $\mathrm{PF}^{\mathrm{et}}_p(E,K_0)$ an isomorphism. This is the counit-adjoint morphism of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] for the source $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K_0$ and target $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}(E\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}p_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}K_0)$. Apply [lem-sfb-unbounded-direct-image-comparison] twice, to $E$ and to $H$, obtaining natural isomorphisms $b_E:A_YRp_{\mathrm{et},*}E\to Rp_*A_{\bar X}E$ and $b_H:A_YRp_{\mathrm{et},*}H\to Rp_*A_{\bar X}H$. Its hypotheses hold: $k$ is algebraically closed, $\ell$ is invertible in $k$, $R$ is finite and $\ell$-primary, and $p$ is finite type (part of properness) between finite-type $k$-schemes. Its statement defines $b$ as the counit mate on all unbounded inputs. In particular it applies to $H$, where the bounded-below comparison would not suffice.

proof.text: Identify the unbounded comparison map with the canonical derived counit mate. First prove the general mate formula in terms of the adjunction homEquiv. Then transport left adjoints from mapDerivedCategory to leftDerivedFunctor and transport the exact comparison functors in the horizontal direction; conjugateEquiv and mateEquiv composition identities show that invertibility is preserved. Expanding the definitions of the derived pullback comparison gives the required square. Apply the existing Adjunction.isIso_rightAdjointProjectionMap_of_mateEquiv to its proved fixed-coefficient tensor compatibility, the etale proper projection formula, and the comparison mates at E and H. Naturality transports the resulting actual pro-etale proper projection to the chosen realizations of j! M and K. This uses the same canonical counit map, rather than an abstract isomorphism of its endpoints.

source.place: Tag 0E48, remark-compatible-with-diagram, applied to the etale/pro-etale comparison square

proof.text: Use [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] with the finite ring $R$, the open immersion $j$, the complex $M$ and $N=Lp^*K$. It makes the exact canonical arrow $\pi_j:j_!M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N\to j_!(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}j^{-1}N)$ invertible on these unbounded categories. The functor $Rp_*$ preserves its inverse. Composing this isomorphism with Step 5 and the pullback composition identification in the statement proves that $\operatorname{PF}_{R;M,K}$ is an isomorphism. Naturality follows directly: each arrow is either the counit of a natural adjunction, a tensor/pullback comparison, or the natural open projection arrow. Their composite is consequently natural in both $M$ and $K$; the origin choices used to establish invertibility add no choices to this composite.

lean.note: The actual canonical compactification projection natural transformation is transported through the published coefficient-realization equivalence into intrinsic constant-ring derived categories. The hypotheses use intrinsic constructibility of each cohomology sheaf and a finite cohomological range, without etale-origin, finite-Tor, flatness or DVR hypotheses. The given open and proper maps are packaged as c.i and c.g in an arbitrary Compactification f, with c.comm recording f = c.i ≫ c.g.
